bars.description: Written bars 1–176, then 181–452: exposition repeat not taken and first ending 177–180 omitted. Bars 1–23 use the encoder's doubled Adagio durations (4/4 rather than the original 4/8), then 2/4 from bar 24. Canonical source extent is 950 quarter units; the performed traversal is 942. This order is subject to fresh recording/source correspondence inspection, not inferred from duration alone.

endpoints.basis: Initial inspection windows for score-pitch energy: the opening lower-string sonority is E3–G3–E4; the last attack is the third separated E-minor closing chord, not its decay. Fresh overlays must establish the precise edges before publication; these windows do not relax any gate.

provenance: The original published MIDI is canonical, not an already repeated performance: every sounding track ends at source q948.5 within the 950-quarter, 452-bar source. The conductor alone carries the exposition volta; named instrumental variables contain the written first and second endings once. String unfoldRepeats expands written tremolos, not an exposition repeat.

Published MIDI track 5 (trombone:) has an unmatched E3/MIDI52 note-off at q856. Regenerate each of the 23 named source instrumental variables on its own MIDI staff, grouping only the resulting source-defined section identities; assert aggregate pitch/onset set equality against the immutable published MIDI before applying the recorded bar order. No malformed MIDI message is silently suppressed and no source part is invented.

Source-declared sounding transpositions are retained: A clarinets; E horns I/II; C horns III/IV changing to E; E/C/E/C trumpets; flute II's brief piccolo change (c'' then c'); and double bass bass_8. The double-bass source begins E3/MIDI52 while cello begins E4/MIDI64 and later reaches low E1/MIDI28; no blanket additional octave lowering is applied. Other parts are non-transposing. Instrument names follow source variables, not MIDI patches.
All timing remains provisional and has not been checked by ear. Source duration warping is not a measured release or a transcription of tremolo/articulation performance.
